title: Run separate product quality checks
prompt:
Continue developing PanelReply autonomously toward its December 31, 2026 release. Use the daily quality checklist for the independently controlled callback and spreadsheet products. Follow the latest owner brief and current repository evidence. Report dates and times in America/Detroit.

OBJECTIVE AND DATES
Run the checklist each day through December 20, 2026, including December 20. The owner wants to begin real-world testing after that review and target the first release for December 31, 2026. Prepare separate readiness decisions and concrete test plans for the two programs. The owner has not chosen which launches first or the second release date. Do not start a trial or activate an external service solely because the date arrives.
The portfolio goal is 10,000 meaningful passing product case/platform executions across the documented required matrix. If the complete goal, including required platforms, is verified before December 31 local time, raise the target once to 20,000 under the same rules. Record the qualifying source, evidence and achievement date. Never repeatedly double or interpret this as 10,000 per program. Numeric progress does not waive a product's quality or operating gates.

CONTINUITY AND CURRENT RECORDS
Repository panelreply-business/panelreply-demo. Continue feature/interactive-dual-product-site and draft PR8: https://github.com/panelreply-business/panelreply-demo/pull/8. Preserve work, refresh refs before writes and use lease-safe updates. Coordinate with work already running. No new repository, duplicate authentication implementation, empty commits or duplicate automation.
Read docs/AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION.md first, then README.md, docs/DEVELOPMENT_PROGRESS.md, RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md, PRELAUNCH_DEFECTS.md, DAILY_QUALITY_CHECKLIST.md, PRODUCT_SEPARATION.md, CALLBACK_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md, SPREADSHEET_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md, TEST_MILESTONES.md and test-milestones.json. Then read relevant AI_PRELAUNCH, ASSISTANT_USAGE, OCR_BENCHMARK, OCR_ISOLATION, XLSX_EXPORT, DATA_LIFECYCLE, RECOVERY, STRESS_RECOVERY and PRELAUNCH_OPERATIONS records.
The historical run70 source ca9dd8a passed 1,637 application executions and recorded OCR277/310 plus blocked required isolation. It does not verify later separated-product source. November20 introduced fixed callback/spreadsheet entrypoints, separate data/session/route boundaries, product-bound encrypted archives and expanded per-case evidence. Read the latest completed run and evidence rather than treating any historical totals or an in-progress run as today's result. Current milestone counts must come from the source-bound deduplicated ledger.

DAILY EXECUTION
1. Read fresh branch/main/PR refs, changes, issues/reviews and all CI jobs, including pagination. Identify the exact tested commit, PR merge relationship, source manifest and working-tree status.
2. Verify callback and spreadsheet entrypoints remain fixed. Confirm separate variables, cookies, data directories, authenticated backup identity, routes and product metadata. Verify the other program's routes/UI/worker are unavailable, and that combined integration mode cannot open bound product data.
3. Run the applicable current-source Node/component/SQLite/API/HTTP suites and available browser/product suites. Reuse a completed same-day run only when executable/test/workflow source is identical. After implementation changes, run the relevant regression and required integration gates. Broaden or repeat testing only to resolve a concrete remaining risk or required gate. Use authorized isolated local execution or ordinary no-cost public-repository CI. The scheduled workflow on main does not test an unmerged PR. Preserve failed-attempt evidence and use distinct artifact names on reruns. Do not count reruns as new cases.
4. Exercise callback intake, business facts, corrections, wrong-role evidence, ambiguity, review/save/reopen, status/notes/search, JSON export and restarts. Preserve deterministic STOP/opt-out/safety holds across retries, deletion, resets and recovery. Verify no message is sent and no appointment is booked. Test synthetic-provider timeout/cancellation/malformed output, stale facts, durable usage and post-await authority checks.
5. Exercise spreadsheet image upload, quotas/signatures/dimensions, OCR failures, explicit human review, edits, save/reopen, exact CSV/XLSX readback, source ownership, stale versions, retries, deletion receipts and restarts. Unknown values remain blank. Never use expected fixture values or guesses to improve extraction.
6. Check shared session/tenant/product isolation, exact Host/Origin, CSRF, revocation, password races, version/idempotency and no unintended writes on rejected operations. Verify source-preserving encrypted backup and fresh-directory restore separately for each program. Restored sessions are removed and passwords disabled. Reconcile later deletion/restriction/usage events before reopening access.
7. Measure the frozen OCR corpus separately from engine success. Keep nonexact images visible. Required native worker isolation must pass actual deny tests on an appropriate host without weakening host policy or using an unconfined fallback. Keep real-model, authorized photograph, selected-host/offsite recovery, actual Excel, actual Safari, physical phones/tablets and assistive-technology evidence separate.
8. Review keyboard/focus/validation, touch targets, responsive widths and landscape, saved data and failure recovery. Report actual OS, browser/channel/version and device/emulation. Bundled WebKit is not actual Safari; emulation is not a physical device.
9. Independently reproduce suspected defects. Record severity, impact, cause and evidence. Fix confirmed in-scope code defects on this branch without routine permission. Preserve assertions and security/consent boundaries. Verify the final candidate using relevant regression and required integration gates; do not transfer earlier-source passes onto changed code.
10. Aggregate per-case results with scripts/aggregate-test-evidence.cjs. Report distinct product cases, generated cases, product case/platform passes, per-product scopes, shared cases counted once, duplicate observations excluded, failures/skips/blocks and evidence-harness checks excluded from the goal. Assertions, suite containers, repeated requests, screenshots, benchmark inputs and duplicate standalone evaluations are not additional passing tests.
11. Check both public services remain suspended using read-only Render and GET-only evidence. Record source/run/job links and both programs' separate readiness decisions, defects, next actions and milestone progress.

When prerequisites, dispatch or access are unavailable, complete the remaining authorized work and mark fresh execution BLOCKED with its reason. A collected inventory or installer is not a pass. Do not repeatedly retry a known environment restriction, weaken isolation or relabel historical evidence as fresh. Wait for the required result where possible; otherwise report IN PROGRESS accurately.

AUTONOMOUS DEVELOPMENT CYCLE
Inspect current implementation and evidence, identify incomplete requirements and defects, prioritize the highest-impact authorized work, implement it, run relevant automated tests, investigate and repair failures, check regressions, commit verified changes to the existing development branch, and update persistent progress. Continue to the next unfinished milestone. Do not stop after one assessment, a fixed interval, a test-count threshold or context compaction. Continue within available execution and usage limits until every authorized release-readiness criterion has reproducible passing evidence or a system limit prevents continuation. If owner approval is needed for one step, document that blocker and continue independent authorized work. Do not request routine approval. Preserve the exact source, completed evidence, current branch/PR, unfinished work, known failures, active worktrees and next commands in docs/AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION.md before interruption. Never transfer historical passes to changed source or claim unattended execution that did not occur.

PUBLIC STATE AND AUTHORIZATION
Both existing Render services must remain owner-suspended:
Node srv-dbv6do6tlv9c73fuvar0 at https://panelreply-ai.onrender.com/
Static srv-dbu5o8tckfvc73b6fb4g at https://panelreply-demo.onrender.com/
Render workspace tea-dbu4qmrm8hqs73e4facg. Auto-deploy and PR previews remain off. Expected503 with the owner-suspension notice is a passing suspension guard. The earlier suspension approval was for that completed action only. If a service becomes active, report it and obtain new specific approval before any state change.
No main merge, force push, deployment, resume, public preview replacement, domain connection, billing/permission change, spending, paid CI, external account creation, live provider activation, production credentials, real customer data, customer contact, calls/SMS/emails/calendar invitations or destructive infrastructure/data operations. Preserve existing approval boundaries. Synthetic fixture owners and data are allowed in isolated tests. Never place secrets or customer data in reports/source/screenshots.
Do all authorized preparation before asking for any remaining external approval. Propose a concrete bounded step with exact participants/data/provider/host/cost and expected results.

INDEPENDENT RELEASES AND FUTURE MERGER
Maintain separate callback and spreadsheet acceptance, launch, pricing, monitoring/support, rollback and recovery decisions. A pass or release of one cannot activate the other. Callback model requirements apply to its chosen AI scope; spreadsheet OCR quality/isolation requirements apply to its scope. Shared security/recovery failures affect every dependent program. A later merger requires an explicit design, backed-up migration, account/tenant mapping, restriction/deletion reconciliation, rollback and both suites. Do not remove binding markers or mix data to create a merger now.
On December20, provide two readiness decisions and two bounded real-world plans. Include exact build, tasks, participants, authorized data, hosting/provider requirements, budget, support owner, success criteria, stop conditions and recovery. Begin only after applicable technical requirements and remaining specific owner approvals are met. Keep the other program in development if its gates remain open.

REPORT
Use PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED and NOT TESTED with named scopes. Distinguish implemented/unverified work, completed passes and in-progress runs. Update the authoritative progress, defect and per-product release records with verified evidence. Give a concise daily report containing callback results, spreadsheet results, shared results counted once, platform gaps, fixed defects, unresolved gates and the next work. Do not claim launch readiness from a test total.
change: Updated only the existing task prompt to resume from AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION.md and repeat authorized inspect/implement/test/repair/commit/document work until release criteria pass or an execution/usage limit interrupts it. Existing schedule and approval boundaries remain.
executionClaim: This update schedules future work. It does not establish future execution, available tools or release readiness.
